column1: # Game profile of BALL x PIT (Switch, update 1.293 = v393216). Plays on the Mac and on the iPhone
# Unity 6000.0.62f1 (IL2CPP) with FMOD and Addressables, SDK 20.5.19; subsdk0 is the movie module. The Shader objects are in the player's serialized files (resources.assets,
# sharedassets1.assets, the built-in resources), which have no type trees, and in 10 of the 11 Addressables bundles (StreamingAssets/aa/Switch), which carry the Shader type tree the others borrow
# (the same type hash), so unityfs.py needs no written-out layout. Needed no host change, as Hollow Knight: Silksong (Unity 6000.0.50f1).
# Docked: the game draws 1280x720 into 1920x1080 window textures and sets the window crop to 1280x720 (nvnWindowSetCrop), at 60 fps. Reads no touch; the 3D pad layout (Input below)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true, and main never sets a heap: Unity 6 takes its memory itself through nn::os::AllocateAddressRegion
# and AllocateMemoryPages in the alias region, as in Hollow Knight: Silksong. The 5 GB block of the other Unity games with virtual address memory, with the node area cut for this sdk build
# (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py). Measured on the Mac over 10 minutes of the first dive and the base: the alias region's high-water mark +2.00 GB of 4.375 GB, 1.26 GB mapped, resident 1.6 GB and
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader and ComputeShader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets bundles (38,099 shaders, 11 of them GLSLC outputs of Unity's player in main)
# In a dive the right stick aims (ZR shoots): the 3D pad layout. It plays with the controller, so it stays docked
